def.brief: Amend two tests cc-tests wrote, before any build, to Q-conflict item 2 as clarified at the end of the contract: test_Q_conflict_eyes_request_fails_clearly_and_writes_no_packet_when_a_section_cannot_be_attributed and test_Q_conflict_verify_packet_excluded_diff_fails_rather_than_returning_partial_text append the foreign 'Submodule x 1111111..2222222:' block after the last section, where it becomes part of that readable section's text; the clarified contract does not validate text inside a readable section. response.summary: I amended the two Q-conflict item-2 tests in test_dwitbuk.py to match the clarified contract. Nothing is committed. They no longer append the 'Submodule x 1111111..2222222:' block after the last section. The `unattributable_git(case)` wrapper now takes a case from a new `UNATTRIBUTABLE` table and each test runs both cases. Case 1 puts the 'Submodule x…' block before the first `diff --git`/`diff --cc` header of a real content diff call's output. Case 2 adds a header of another kind, 'diff --unknown x', with a line under it, after the last readable section. The assertions are unchanged: in `eyes request` the exit code is non-zero, the message is clear and no eyes-request.json is written; `verify_packet` fails instead of returning `excluded_diff` text. `clear_about_it` also accepts a message that names 'diff --unknown', since the new case has no 'Submodule x' text to quote. I checked with a focused python3 -c run of each test in each case, and all four fail on the current tree for the right reason. `eyes request` exits 0 and writes a packet in both cases. `verify_packet` returns the notes.json section as `excluded_diff` in both cases; in case 2 the 'diff --unknown x' block is joined onto it.
